You can reach incredibly high precision in studies with sample sizes that are a fraction of a fraction of the size you would ostensibly expect. You can find the confidence interval in most any study is going to be at the 95% level. What this means is that any identical study would be expected, with 95% certainty, that have identical results within a certain interval. This is mathematically measured using the variance of the sample - the lower the variance in results, the lower the sample size needed for accuracy.

Published research doesn't just get published. It goes through a peer review process and basic things like sample selection/size are considered obviously heavily considered.
